verdicts.strongest_argument: Everything factual here is the company's own five-month-old disclosure, published, stored in this capture, and structurally known. The guidance suspension, the Section 232 amendment mechanics and the 'in excess of $500M for the remainder of the year, before any mitigation measures' figure all come from the 2026-04-15 release and sit in docs/07166c5ce4d72f772ffef77207bc045b50a8ec47.txt, indexed in snapshots/20260830T084024Z.json item 1 (admissible per clean-view), at entries dated 2026-04-15. That an issuer without a guide must either reinstate one or explain at its next scheduled release is not information - it is the calendar, and it was equally true of the 2026-05-28 release, which the finding's own independence field notes beat with a 'stronger outlook despite tariff pressures' and traded up 7.4% pre-market. So the market has already run this exact test once, in public, and the answer was mitigation. Age is not novelty. The genuinely useful part of this finding is not an unpriced fact at all but a correction to the baseline: the 2.19% median is computed from six 6-Ks matched by text on a 36-day inferred cadence, which the baseline itself flags as cadence_implausible, so the expected move for a real quarterly print is materially wider. That is a measurement critique, not an edge, and it cuts both ways. I also reject the supporting inference - 'the market has quietly assumed the $500M is largely mitigable because the stock is only 22.5% off its high' - as run-up-as-evidence, and note it is self-undermining: if the market has assumed mitigation, then the market has taken a view, which is pricing.
